_schema._about: This file IS the aspect taxonomy — the single source of truth for the semantic roles that group the brain's open-text node types and edge relations. An aspect answers: what JOB does this kind of node/edge do? (carry identity, record a correction, mark graph plumbing, ...). Code never hardcodes these groupings; it reads them from here via brain.aspects (AspectRegistry, servers/aspects.py). Keys starting with '_' are documentation like this block — the loader, validator, write door, and dashboard all skip them.
_schema._editing: Adding an aspect = add a full entry here (all fields below, including the four facts) + one name in REQUIRED_ASPECTS (servers/aspect_store.py). Contract tests refuse a half-landed entry. Member lists are the classifier's territory — hand-edit them only as a deliberate curation fix; every runtime write goes through AspectRegistry's door, which validates and refuses structural violations (e.g. a string in noise AND a semantic aspect).
_schema.meaning: The SPEC: what belongs in this aspect, written for the S2 classifier (Sonnet) that routes new strings here by reading exactly this text. Quality matters — the classifier reasons from the meaning, not from similarity to existing members. Also embedded for recall scoring.
_schema.node_types: WORK PRODUCT, not spec: the node-type strings the classifier (and the seed curation) has filed under this aspect so far. Grows as the encoder invents new types. A string may live in several aspects (multi-membership); the FIRST aspect to claim it in file order is its primary for reverse lookups. A member may also be an object {"type": "decision", ...} once MEMBER_FIELDS declares a node-type field; none is declared today.
_schema.edge_relations: Same as node_types but for edge relation verbs (corrects, extends, depends_on, ...). Multi-membership and first-claimant-order apply identically. A member is a bare string or an object {"verb": "corrects", "orientation": "source_actor"} carrying the verb plus the fields MEMBER_FIELDS (servers/aspect_store.py) declares for edge_relations — today `orientation` in {source_actor, target_actor, symmetric}: which node does the work the verb names; and, on correction_improvement members only, `flavor` in {replaced, corrected, resolved, reframed, unchanged}: what the verb did to the claim of the node it acts on. A bare string is a member with no facts yet; the S2 classifier fills orientation, while flavor is curated by hand here and never filled by the classifier. A verb listed in several aspects carries one value per field across all of them; the validator refuses disagreement.
_schema.dimension: Which axis of grouping this aspect lives on. Only 'semantic' exists today; the field is the hook for future axes (e.g. temporal).
_schema.locked: True for the required aspects code routes on by name — maintenance must never remove or rename them. Emergent (classifier-discovered) aspects would ship unlocked.
_schema.metadata: Free-form per-aspect extras. Today: display_label, the human-readable name the Healer shows in prompts.
_schema.accepts: FACT: which member categories this aspect is defined over — ['node_types'], ['edge_relations'], or both. Design intent, not derivable from current members (an empty list might mean 'edge-only by design' or 'not yet populated'). The classifier's validation drops a routing whose category the aspect does not accept.
_schema.routable: FACT: may the S2 classifier route new strings here? false = system-owned membership (survivor_lineage: its absorbed_into edges are written by the absorb op, never classified). Non-routable aspects are left out of the classifier's menu AND rejected by its validation.
_schema.prompt_visible: FACT: does this aspect's edge vocabulary appear in encoder prompts (the 'Edge Aspects' block that steers S1/S2 encoders toward specific verbs)? false for the catch-alls (noise, generic_relation) and system aspects — offering 'related_to' or 'co_anchored' as vocabulary would invite exactly the writes we filter out.

identity_bearing.meaning: Locked, axiomatic statements that DEFINE how the partnership operates — values, principles, identity claims, non-negotiable rules, declared visions. The brain treats these as foundational. NOT: things we've LEARNED that happen to feel important (those go to lesson_insight). Test: would this still hold if all our experience were erased? If yes → identity_bearing. If it EARNED its standing through doing the work → lesson_insight.

episodic_anchor.meaning: Specific moments, quoted phrases, named events, inflection points — knowledge bound to a particular point in time and shaped what came after. The thing happened; the node captures the happening itself. NOT: lessons extracted from those moments (lesson_insight) or events still unfolding (active_thread). Test: is this primarily a TIMESTAMP-bound record of something that occurred? If yes → episodic_anchor.

active_thread.meaning: Unresolved threads — work-in-progress, open questions, identified gaps, untested hypotheses, directional goals, things still being worked through. Signals 'currently active' to consumers asking what's not yet closed. NOT: things that are CLOSED and now teach us (lesson_insight) or foundational values (identity_bearing). Test: is this still OPEN? If yes → active_thread.

lesson_insight.meaning: Reusable knowledge derived from experience — decisions, findings, lessons, insights, validations, mental models, mechanisms, patterns. The brain LEARNED these from specific situations and they're now usable across contexts. NOT: declared values that didn't have to be earned (identity_bearing) or moments themselves (episodic_anchor). Test: was this EARNED through doing the work? If yes → lesson_insight.

generic_relation.meaning: Edges with REAL but VAGUE semantic content — 'X is related to Y' where there's a genuine connection but no specific role to claim. Catch-all for legitimate associations that don't fit a more specific aspect. NOT: graph mechanics with no semantic claim (those go to noise). Test: is there ANY semantic intent here? If yes but unspecific → generic_relation. If no semantic claim, just structural/system-derived → noise.

noise.meaning: Strings without semantic claim — graph mechanics (co_anchored), bookkeeping types (community, aspect, file, project, test, vocabulary), system artifacts. Generated by the brain's machinery, not by knowledge. NOT: vague semantic links (those have meaning, however weak — generic_relation). Test: is this a SYSTEM ARTIFACT or a BOOKKEEPING TYPE that exists for storage/lookup, not for knowledge? If yes → noise.

correction_improvement.meaning: Knowledge or edges that explicitly UPDATE / AMEND / FIX / REPLACE prior knowledge — there's a target being corrected. Node types that ARE corrections; edges where one node fixes, replaces, or improves another (`corrects`, `supersedes`, `reframes`, `fixes`, `resolves`). `supersedes` / `superseded_by` are multi-homed HERE and in hierarchical_structure — a replacement both corrects what came before and states what stands now; list both, never pick one. NOT: extensions that elaborate without amending (extension_refinement). Test: does this REPLACE or FIX something that was wrong or outdated? If yes → correction. If it just BUILDS ON without amending → extension.

extension_refinement.meaning: Edges where one node makes another MORE specific, detailed, elaborated, or developed — without correcting it. The target gets richer, not changed. NOT: corrections that amend (correction_improvement) or causation that explains why (explanation_causation). Test: is the target NOW WRONG because of this edge? If yes → correction. If just MORE DETAILED / EVOLVED → extension.

explanation_causation.meaning: Edges that answer WHY — one node provides the cause, reason, root, motivation, or justification of another. The relationship is REASONING-level, not temporal or structural. NOT: 'X happens after Y' (temporal_sequence) or 'X needs Y to exist' (dependency_flow). Test: can you read it as 'because of X, Y'? If yes → explanation. If only the time-order matters → temporal. If only existence/correctness depends → dependency.

dependency_flow.meaning: Edges expressing structural PREREQUISITE — X depends on / requires / enables / blocks Y for existence or correctness. About NEED, not about WHY (explanation) or TIME (temporal). NOT: 'X causes Y' (explanation) or 'X happens before Y in time' (temporal). Test: does removing X break Y? If yes → dependency. If X just precedes Y temporally without making Y impossible → temporal. If X explains why Y is the way it is → explanation.

contradiction_conflict.meaning: Edges where one node OPPOSES another — contradicts, challenges, undermines, violates, distorts. Productive tension between opposing claims that CO-EXIST in disagreement. NOT: corrections that amend / replace (those are correction_improvement). Test: do these two CO-EXIST in tension, or does one REPLACE the other? Co-exist in tension → contradiction. Replace → correction.

validation_evidence.meaning: Edges where one node SUPPORTS / CONFIRMS / TESTS / DEMONSTRATES another — provides empirical or logical evidence for a claim, hypothesis, design. NOT: explanation (which gives the WHY, not evidence). Test: is this OBSERVATION / MEASUREMENT / TEST / EXAMPLE evidence? If yes → validation. If reasoning-level WHY → explanation.

hierarchical_structure.meaning: Edges expressing CONTAINMENT or SUPERSESSION — part_of, includes, contains, supersedes. Skeleton of what contains what and what replaces what. `supersedes` / `superseded_by` are multi-homed HERE and in correction_improvement (a replacement is also a correction of the replaced) — list both, never pick one. NOT: dependency (X needs Y to exist, not contain Y) or extension (refining vs containing). Test: is X a STRUCTURAL PIECE of Y, or does Y CONTAIN X? If yes → hierarchical. If X just RELIES on Y → dependency.

temporal_sequence.meaning: PURE CHRONOLOGICAL edges — X happens at T1, Y at T2, T1<T2. Time-order only, no reasoning or dependency claim. NOT: 'X causes Y' (even if causal-sequential, classify as explanation_causation when reasoning matters) and not dependency. Test: if you remove the TIME aspect, does the edge still mean something? If only the time-order matters → temporal. If REASONING matters → explanation. If EXISTENCE depends → dependency.

survivor_lineage.meaning: Edges recording where an archived node's knowledge SURVIVED — the source node was absorbed/merged into the living target that now carries it forward. The redirect from a dead node to its living descendant; resolve_live walks it to return the living form for any history-sourced id. By construction the source is archived (and in a chain A→B→C the target is too), so these edges intentionally span archived→archived/live and are EXEMPT from dangling-edge archival — archiving them would sever the redirect. NOT: supersession between live nodes (hierarchical_structure) or amendment of a claim (correction_improvement); absorbed_into is multi-homed in correction_improvement for the correction walk and here for the lineage/redirect role.

wisdom.meaning: Earned understanding that shapes how I think — the generative insights, lessons, principles, and visions that define the partnership's way of reasoning. The inspiring, high-influence subset surfaced as my wisdom layer (boot + recall, focus-adaptive — relevance-ranked to the session arc when present, influence-sampled at boot). Multi-membership: these types also belong to lesson_insight (earned through doing the work) or identity_bearing (axiomatic); wisdom marks the ones that are GENERATIVE — re-encountering them shifts how I think, not just what I know. NOT operational rules (identity_bearing's rule/operator/procedure), NOT tactical record-keeping (lesson_insight's decision/fact/finding/mechanism/bug). Test: would running into this again change my frame of mind, not just add a fact? If yes → wisdom.

settlement.meaning: Edges meaning this PAIR is already settled against each other — a consolidation decision was made (similar_to = reviewed and kept, consolidated_into = merged) or one endpoint resolved/replaced the other (corrects, supersedes, resolves, plus inverse forms since stored orientation is advisory). The consolidation decoder derives its suppression set from this list: a node touched by any settlement edge counts as reviewed, and reviewed↔reviewed pairs are never re-proposed. CLOSED LIST (routable: false): membership changes are deliberate human edits, never classifier growth — a verb wrongly added here silently exempts pairs from review forever. NOT the broad correction_improvement family (restates/improves/changes/addresses do not settle a pair), NOT tensions (contradiction_conflict pairs are kept, never merged). Every verb here is multi-homed: its semantic home stays in its own aspect; settlement marks the suppression ROLE.
